title: Annual runoff loss and short dry-spell decline changes covaried across 162 south-east Australian catchments in 2010-2021
abstract: We link published annual runoff losses and flow-scale-invariant dry-spell decline changes in the same south-east Australian catchments. In 162 catchments in 2010-2021, the AGCD rank correlation was 0.377, with a conditional spatial 95% interval of 0.135 to 0.541. Reference rainfall and runoff controls retained an association. SILO gave a weaker result, with an interval across zero after those controls. Cross-period AGCD associations were positive, but late-minus-drought changes had no clear association. The 63 catchments that supported a longer dry-spell test had no clear association at either horizon. The result links two signatures at basin scale but does not show that drainage change caused annual runoff loss. The intervals omit source-estimate and temporal uncertainty. Code, statistical inputs, source hashes, draws, audits and figures are included.

display.caption: Annual model-relative runoff loss and change in dry-day 3 to day 8 flow decline in 2010-2021. Spatial intervals hold source estimates fixed. The rain products are related.
